A wild, emotionally rich, and insightful look at free thinkers who took an inspirational stand.
Thanks to its thoughtful protagonists and filmmaker Jeremy Workman, what starts out as a quirky human interest story becomes a profoundly humane portrait of creativity and community.
Secret Mall Apartment, then, is an engaging and thoughtful examination of a thorny piece of performance, one made even thornier by the movie’s own existence.
What began as a kind of self congratulatory, anti-establishment rebel yell, the collective became a family that gave back to the community.  But how long could it last?

Whether you view [it] as a bit of commentary or just a light hearted rib, either way, you’re right. Secret Mall Apartment profiles people who created a work of disruptive art that creates an emotional connection by not being traditionally disruptive.
Astonishing. About the charm and the fanciful ideas that make life great. One of the best films of the year.

A rare doc gem that on the surface seems simple (pranksters carving a secret space in a behemoth mall), but underneath are themes of gentrification, commerce, authority and especially the debate of "what is art?" Hell, what is life? W/director interview.
